title: Nat port exhaustion: host NIC teardown causing eviction loop and slow recovery
content:
Summary:
We observed a tier of mixed-instance worker nodes entering an eviction loop across several clusters starting 2025-02-14 03:40 UTC. Pod restarts and PodStartup latencies spiked for latency-sensitive services. Root cause appears to be a cascade: host NIC (ebpf-managed) went through a transient teardown after a kernel firmware update step, left ephemeral NAT ports in TIME_WAIT / unreusable state and the node's conntrack/NAT tables effectively exhausted for the node's nat range. Kubelet started evicting pods aggressively to free resources; evictions caused many ephemeral ports to be opened/closed and exacerbated the exhaustion. Recovery was slow because the node-level NAT allocations did not reclaim quickly and kube-proxy/ipvs rules were briefly inconsistent during NIC reattachment.

Impact and scope:
- Affected clusters: us-west-2-prod and us-west-2-staging (subset of worker pools using mixed-instance family and custom NIC firmware agent).
- Affected services: request-facing microservices (sustained 5–20% error rate increase), batch jobs saw increased retries, scheduled cron jobs delayed by up to 30m.
- Time window: 2025-02-14 03:40 UTC -> partial stabilization 2025-02-14 06:10 UTC, full rollback/cleanup 2025-02-14 08:00 UTC.
- Customer-visible impact: intermittent 500/502 rate on a small percentage of traffic (SLA unaffected for most customers but degraded for some endpoints).

Detection:
- Pager triggered by cluster-p95 pod startup latency alert (threshold breached at 03:45 UTC).
- Grafana panel "node ephemeral ports / conntrack usage" jumped to >95% capacity on multiple nodes.
- On-call Slack thread: #sre-oncall -> channel noise detecting rapid node OutOfResources eviction events.

Timeline (high level):
- 03:40 UTC: first pod startup latencies spike; kubelet reports Eviction Thresholds exceed for memory + ephemeral ports heuristic.
- 03:42 UTC: SRE alert: node-level conntrack usage > 90% in pool-mix-3.
- 03:50 UTC: Automated remediation attempted: cordon+drain of affected nodes launched by autoscaler (partial).
- 04:05 UTC: We manually reprovisioned a node without NIC agent to validate: fresh node did not show NAT exhaustion.
- 04:45 UTC: Observed many TIME_WAIT sockets and NAT translations with long extant timers; kernel netfilter conntrack entries in STALE state.
- 05:10 UTC: Applied temporary mitigation: increase net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max and lowered nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait on affected nodes via SSH-backed bootstrap (config daemon) to accelerate reclamation.
- 06:10 UTC: Pod evictions slowed; services started returning to nominal error rates.
- 08:00 UTC: Full cleanup by rolling replace of nodes in pool plus a fix deployed to NIC agent (stop aggressive firmware stage).

Investigation notes:
- Nodes impacted had the NIC firmware orchestrator agent newly rolled out in the previous maintenance window. That agent triggers a soft-restart of the NIC stack to apply micro-updates; in a subset this generated a transient interface teardown that left NAT translations in an inconsistent state for the node.
- Kube-proxy ipvs rules were reinstalled on NIC reattachment but some ephemeral translations were left relying on old conntrack entries, creating duplicate mappings and preventing new ephemeral port allocations for outbound SNAT.
- Evictions accelerated NAT churn: pods evicted -> new pods scheduled on other nodes -> outbound connections use new ephemeral ports -> reach NAT allocation limit repeatedly.
- Observed kernel params on impacted nodes had conservative TIME_WAIT timeout (600s) and low nf_conntrack_max relative to pod density (value 524288).
- We found one utility (internal: nic-monitor) logging repeated "netdev down -> up" cycles for the NIC during the agent run.

Root cause hypothesis:
Primary: NIC agent triggered soft teardown leaving conntrack/NAT state inconsistent and exhausting ephemeral port namespace under normal traffic patterns.
Contributing: nf_conntrack parameters were not sized for the higher pod density of mixed-instance pool; kubelet eviction thresholds treated ephemeral port pressure via net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse heuristics poorly (no direct metric previously).

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Increased nf_conntrack_max on affected nodes via a rolling SSH script (short-term).
- Reduced TIME_WAIT via lowering nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait (conservative numbers to reduce backlog).
- Cordon+drain of worst nodes and perform rolling replace to ensure NIC agent not run until we have a patch.
- Applied temporary iptables rule to drop stale conntrack entries older than 20 minutes for the nat table (scripted, conservative).

Permanent mitigations and action items:
1) NIC agent fix: change firmware micro-update flow to avoid soft teardown; add explicit conntrack flush+reinstall hook when interface restarts. (Owner: infra-networking, JIRA SRE-3145)
2) Update cluster bootstrap to increase nf_conntrack_max and tune TIME_WAIT for high-density pools; make this configurable per node-pool. (Owner: cluster-provisioning)
3) Add a synthetic monitor: node-level ephemeral-port utilization and a metric exported via node-exporter. Alert when >70% for >5m. (Owner: observability)
4) Update eviction heuristic: add a signal for ephemeral-port pressure to kubelet autoscaler policy so we can prefer cordon+drain earlier. (Owner: eng-sre + platform)
5) Implement a safe conntrack cleanup playbook (runbook below) and automate via daemon when safe. (Owner: eng-sre)
6) Run density test matrix for mixed-instance pools to ensure nf_conntrack sizing baseline. (Owner: perf)

Runbook (fast path) - for oncall SREs:
1) Detection: Grafana query -> node_netstat_conntrack_used / node_netstat_conntrack_max > 0.75 across > 3 nodes in same pool; p95 PodStartupLatency > threshold.
2) Short-term mitigation: cordon the top 3 worst nodes (kubectl cordon <node>), drain non-critical pods; prefer to drain stateful sets slowly.
3) If cordon+drain not sufficient: set net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to +25% (sysctl -w) and reduce nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait to 120s temporarily.
4) If still impacted: roll nodes out of pool (replace) with nodes that do not run NIC agent, and scale up a safe pool.
5) After nodes are healthy: run conntrack -L | grep <pattern> to identify stale entries; run conntrack -D --orig-dport <port> only after confirming safe target. Prefer scripted cleanup: /usr/local/bin/conntrack-cleanup --older-than 1200s --dry-run then run for real.
6) Communicate: post status to #sre-oncall with affected pools, estimated time to recovery, and customer impact summary.

Monitoring / Queries (examples to add to playbook):
- Prometheus: sum(node_conntrack_entries) by (node) / sum(node_conntrack_max) by (node)
- Grafana panel: topk(10, node_conntrack_entries) with node labels
- kubectl: kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Node -n kube-system --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 200
- conntrack: conntrack -S to show counters; conntrack -L | wc -l

Post-incident checklist (owners assigned):
- infra-networking: implement NIC agent change + deploy canary (due 2025-02-21).
- cluster-provisioning: baseline nf_conntrack_max per node-type and publish recommended sizes (due 2025-02-20).
- observability: add ephemeral-port utilization alert and dashboard (due 2025-02-18).
- eng-sre: formalize conntrack safe-clean playbook and automation with appropriate safety checks (due 2025-02-19).
- perf: run density test and publish results (due 2025-02-28).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How many other node pools run the NIC agent in the same aggressive mode? Need an inventory.
- Is there a feasible kernel backport/setting that allows faster TIME_WAIT reclamation w/o breaking long-lived tcp assumptions? (sync with kernel team)
- Could kube-proxy be made more resilient to NIC flaps by proactively recreating SNAT chains? (platform investigation)

Notes to self / oncall scribbles (informal):
- saw Node ip-10-1-23-45.us internal show 94% conntrack; conntrack -L | head -> lots of dport collisions.
- local test: restarting the nic-monitor service on a dev node produced same pattern (teardown -> stale nat entries). Good repro.
- caution: aggressive conntrack deletion can break long-lived connections; rely on cordon+drain first.

Related tickets / links:
- JIRA-SRE-3145: NIC agent: avoid interface soft-teardown (tracking)
- GH issue: github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-ops/issue/209 - conntrack cleanup helper
- Confluence: Node networking playbook (link above)

Appendix: quick sysctl snippets used during mitigation (for runbook copy/paste)
- sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=786432
- sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait=120
- conntrack --cleanup --older-than 1200  # (internal helper used with care)

End of draft.

Unresolved: need to check whether the NIC vendor logs indicate any firmware crash that correlates exactly with the 03:40 UTC window; ask infra-networking to pull NIC agent debug bundle.
